**Question:** How long may a single command take before it counts as too slow? (SC-001)

**Why it matters:** The 600,000-iteration hashing just agreed costs roughly 0.2–0.3 s per password check, so SC-004's 50-registration persistence test will run for something like half a minute — without a stated budget there is no way to tell a correctly slow run from a performance bug.

**Recommended:** Option A — a 1-second ceiling per command leaves roughly 3× headroom over the expected derivation cost on ordinary hardware, so the budget catches a genuine regression (an accidental re-derivation loop, a repeated full-file reparse) without failing on a slow machine.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | ≤1 s per command on ordinary hardware; whole test suite ≤60 s |
| B | ≤2 s per command; suite ≤120 s — more tolerance for slow or shared CI hardware |
| C | No performance target stated; speed is explicitly out of scope for this feature |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
